Subject: Internal: Tempest redline — legal recommendation

Soojin / Aditya — quick legal take after reviewing Tempest's redline (attached evidence checklist). Key points and recommended language: 

1) Defense vs. Reimbursement: Redwood can accept defense/control for third-party claims alleging IP infringement of customer data or content generated by the model if: 
   - Redwood has the right to select counsel and control defense; customer cooperation required and not unreasonably withheld;
   - Redwood may not settle any claim that admits fault or imposes ongoing obligations on customer without customer's prior written consent;
   - Customer may take over defense for injunctive relief where injunctive relief is the primary remedy and provide indemnity for Redwood's reasonable fees in that instance.

2) Evidence / notice: We should require the customer to provide the claim notice, sample prompts/outputs, and any DMCA or patent notices within 10 business days. Without timely evidence we reserve the right to limit indemnity. See attached evidence_checklist.csv for suggested fields.

3) Cap and insurance: Suggest a commercial cap tied to the order value and an explicit insurance representation; offer to increase cap where customer procures specified insurance (e.g., IP infringement coverage).

4) Timeline for responses: Commit to initial acknowledgement within 3 business days and status updates every 14 days for active matters — that's reasonable.

I'll prepare tracked language for the MSA that implements the above. Recommend we share the proposal with Tempest before contracting call to speed the meeting.

Attachments:
- evidence_checklist.csv (csv) — proposed list of evidence items and format

—Kim

Helen — appreciate the quick turnaround. Two commercial data points from our side to help trade through defense control:

1) If Redwood accepts control of defense (with the limited injunctive carveout Kim suggests), we would need either: (a) a higher liability cap (we typically propose 2x ARR for IP claims) OR (b) an explicit insurance requirement (evidence of IP insurance with $X limits).

2) We can commit to the notification and update cadence Kim outlined (ack in 3 business days, updates every 14 days).

If you can confirm Tempest's appetite on cap vs. insurance, we can incorporate the tradeoff into the draft language and have Kim share tracked edits prior to the call. Can you do a 30-min call today at 3pm PT?

Aditya / Soojin / Kim — thanks, got it. A couple quick counterpoints from Tempest Legal: 

- Tempest wants to preserve the right to select counsel for injunctive relief (we can accept Redwood selecting counsel for purely monetary claims).
- We are open to an insurance requirement. Tempest can procure IP insurance, but it will likely be vendor-specific coverage; can you outline the minimum limits you would require (we propose $2M as a starting point).
- We want the evidence appendix as requested. We also asked that any surveillance of privileged communications be explicitly prohibited in the carveout language.

We'll take the commercial tradeoff back to our procurement team (cap vs insurance) and come back. Also — can Redwood provide a short "claim playbook" describing the steps Redwood will take once notice is received? That would help our internal ops team and speed triage.

Subject: Next steps — Tempest indemnity path and deliverables

Team / Helen — summary and agreed path forward from our side so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Defense/control: Redwood will accept defense/control for third-party IP infringement claims subject to: Redwood selection of counsel, customer's right to take over defense for injunctive relief, no settlement admitting customer's fault without consent.

2) Commercial tradeoff: If Tempest provides evidence of an IP insurance policy meeting the minimum limits ($2M), Redwood will accept a lower cap (1x ARR floor). If Tempest cannot provide insurance, Redwood will propose a higher cap (2x ARR) — final number to be put in the order form.

3) Evidence & timing: Tempest to provide claim notice and the items in our evidence checklist within 10 business days of notice. Redwood will ack within 3 business days and provide status updates every 14 days.

4) Playbook & redline: Kim has prepared tracked MSA language implementing the above. I've attached a compiled redline that incorporates our recommended positions. We will also produce a short claim playbook (1–2 pages) describing roles, contact points, timelines, and initial steps for triage.

Action items: 
- Tempest: confirm whether you will meet the $2M insurance minimum or prefer the cap route (reply by EOD Tue).
- Kim: finalize tracked redline and playbook for Tempest review (Kim target: Wed COB).
- Aditya / Soojin: schedule executive procurement touchpoint once Tempest confirms insurance vs cap.

Attachments:

I will open INF-983 in Jira and attach the final redline and playbook; will share the link when complete. Thanks all — looking forward to wrapping this before procurement week.
